channel.title: Open Calls for Artists — Monographica
channel.description: Curated list of open calls for photographers and visual artists. Exhibitions, grants, residencies, and publications worldwide.

item.title: The Butterfly Effect — SaveArtSpace Billboard Exhibition
item.description: Public art exhibition on billboard advertising space in New York City, curated by Skip Brea, opening October 30, 2026. Themed Stories and Movements, The Butterfly Effect reflects on the moments that have shaped us — the stories we have heard, the experiences we carry, the sounds we listen to and the ones we still hope to encounter — and treats all the arts as sources of movement and memory, from the rhythms and lyrics that transport or connect us to those that mark a particular time in a life. The organisers frame the theme around the energy, uncertainty and possibility of moving through the world, as well as the stories that stay long after the moments have passed. Open to artists of all ages and talents; the application form takes still JPEGs only and excludes corporate logos, personal advertising and video, so photographic work is eligible. Submissions run August 24 to September 21, 2026, selected artists are announced after October 5, and the work goes up on NYC ad space for at least one month. SaveArtSpace is a 501(c)(3) non-profit and fees are tax-deductible donations that pay for the ad space. — Deadline: September 21, 2026. Fee: $35 (1–3 images), $10 each additional. Prize: Billboard exhibition in NYC.

item.title: Halloran Contemporary Art Prize 2027 · Jervis Bay Maritime Museum
item.description: An acquisitive art prize at the Jervis Bay Maritime Museum on the NSW South Coast that engages with and responds to the museum's Halloran Collection: Science & the Sea. For 2027 entrants must explore the theme 'Between Light and Reason' in a new work created for the prize, and the entry declaration requires that the work has not been previously exhibited. First Place takes $20,000 and is acquired by the museum, with $5,000 for the Runner-Up and a $2,000 People's Choice award, a $27,000 pool that makes this one of the larger regional awards in the state. Open to permanent residents of NSW or the ACT aged over 18; entry is $50 per artwork and each artwork needs its own submission form. No medium restriction appears on either public surface — the entry form takes the medium as free text — and the museum's own 2025 finalist catalogue lists a digital photograph and a digital print among the selected works, so photographic entries compete. Work offered for sale carries a 30% museum commission. The full 2027 guidelines and terms pack is sent on request through a form on the museum's website. Entries close 5pm on Monday 30 November 2026, and no late submissions are accepted. — Deadline: November 30, 2026. Fee: A$50 per artwork. Prize: A$20,000 acquisitive + A$5,000 + A$2,000.

item.title: 38th NSA National Online Juried Show
item.description: The National Society of Artists' 38th annual juried show, run entirely online: nothing is shipped to a venue, and every juried work is displayed and offered for sale on OnlineGalleryShows.com from October 4 to December 4, 2026. NSA is a 501(c)(3) founded in 1985 and based in Texas, set up for artists working across all media rather than one, and it names photography alongside painting, drawing, computer-generated art and sculpture. Amanda Barry Jones is the juror. Awards total $1,850 in cash: $750 Best of Show, $500 first, $250 second, $100 third, two $50 Honorable Mentions (the second at the juror's discretion) and the $150 Gay & Philip G. Paratore Memorial Award. Open to artists in the United States and Canada working in 2D or 3D; work must be original, made within the last three years, never accepted into a previous NSA national show, and offered for sale for the run of the exhibition. AI work is not accepted and the show is family-friendly, so no nudes, gory violence or obscene work. Entry is $35 for the first submission and $15 for each additional with no cap on submissions, though a maximum of three works per artist can be juried in. Sales are split artist 65%, NSA 20%, OnlineGalleryShows 15%, and artists ship sold work themselves, unframed and freight-free within the continental US. Notifications go out by September 28. — Deadline: September 19, 2026. Fee: $35 (first entry), $15 each additional. Prize: $1,850 in cash awards.

item.title: A4 International Residency Program 2027–2028 · A4 Residency Art Center
item.description: The A4 Residency Art Center in Chengdu has hosted 335 creators from more than 44 countries and regions since 2011, and its open call is running for the 2028 cycles — Spring 2028 (April–June) and Autumn 2028 (July–October), each lasting roughly eight weeks and adjustable to the project. Two tracks are offered. The fully funded International Residency Fellowship provides a private studio and living quarters, round-trip economy airfare or second-class rail within a set budget, and an RMB 10,000 production grant per project, plus access to the centre's resource network, media promotion, and presentation of the outcome through exhibitions, performances, publications or public art projects. A self-funded 'Light Version' gives the same studio, accommodation and platform access but leaves travel and production costs to the artist. Applications are welcomed from multidisciplinary artists including but not limited to visual arts, performing arts, music, film, sound and architecture, as well as curators and designers; the centre's own past-resident roster is full of photographers, tagged as such year after year. Residents are asked to initiate one or two participatory local events, and each is paired with a local 'Super Agent' to help them read the city and the community. Selection weighs originality, cross-disciplinary collaboration, feasibility, and social and cultural impact. Apply free by email with a personal photo, portfolio, CV and project proposal, all submitted in both English and Chinese. The 2027 round closed on 30 June 2026; the deadline for the 2028 all-year recruitment is 31 December 2026. — Deadline: December 31, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: RMB 10,000 grant + Funded residency.

item.title: Power Plant Grant 2026 · Big Car Collaborative
item.description: Five $12,000 project grants for visual artists who live in Indiana, run by the Indianapolis non-profit Big Car Collaborative — the organisation behind the Contemporary Art Museum of Indianapolis — with funding from the Andy Warhol Foundation for the Visual Arts' Regional Regranting Program. Photography is named outright among the eligible practices, alongside painting, drawing, sculpture, book art, ceramics, fiber, printmaking, digital and media works, film, video, performance art, sound art and social practice. The programme backs new, public-facing projects that happen in unexpected places, challenge mainstream methods of thinking, making or presenting, and build new kinds of audiences; it will not fund conventional private studio work, and equipment purchase, studio rent, travel or professional fees cannot be a proposal's sole or primary purpose. Applicants must be over 21 at the time of application and may not be full-time students; awarded artists should remain Indiana residents for the whole award period. Teams, partnerships and unincorporated individuals are eligible, non-profits and artist-run spaces are not, and previous recipients must wait two years. Eligibility recently widened from the Indianapolis area to the whole state, and Big Car's own venues cannot host a funded project. Applications close November 20, 2026 at 11:59pm EST; ten finalists give a virtual project presentation on December 11 and grantees are announced December 18, with the grant period running January to December 2027. Free to apply, with virtual info sessions through October. — Deadline: November 20, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $12,000.

item.title: Dora Maar House Fellowship 2027
item.description: One- to two-month residencies at the Dora Maar House in Ménerbes, Provence, offered since 2007 to mid-career arts and humanities professionals. Fellows get a private bedroom and bath, a study or studio, a $1,500 stipend and a travel award set at the average fare from their home to Paris; the residency itself costs nothing. The house holds four private bedrooms, three studies for writers and scholars, a studio for artists and a piano, with a shared kitchen, library, living and dining rooms and two gardens. This is explicitly not a residence for emerging creatives — the DMCC says most residents have already published, had several solo exhibitions, particularly in non-commercial spaces, or made a feature film — and photographers are among the alumni. Fellows are asked to make one public presentation at the monthly Salons, held March to November, to be good neighbours in Ménerbes, and to donate one work made during the stay. There is one admission cycle a year, March 15 to October 15, for residencies the following March through November; applications go through SlideRoom in French or English and fellows need a basic knowledge of one of the two. Visual artists submit ten captioned images alongside a CV of no more than four pages, a project description of up to 1,000 words, one letter of reference and an idea of what they would offer the village. Applications are reviewed by the Director, the jury and the board of directors, and applicants hear back roughly two and a half months after the deadline. On the application fee the organisation's own two surfaces disagree: the Apply page states $25, while the SlideRoom portal prices the live 2027 DMCC Residency Program at $12. — Deadline: October 15, 2026. Fee: $12. Prize: $1,500 stipend + Residency.

item.title: Purple · Midwest Center for Photography
item.description: The next themed show in the Midwest Center for Photography's colour series, following Yellow: an international call for photographs that represent the hue purple. MWCP frames it as the colour lying between blue and red on the spectrum — the one most associated with royalty, passion and softness — and asks for work spanning the dark richness of deep chroma through to light, airy violet and lavender. Open to all photographers internationally. Each photograph is judged on the merit of the individual image; series-based entries are not necessary and a range of different images is preferred. Selected artists have their work featured in the gallery in Wichita, Kansas and online, January 9–25, 2027. The early entry deadline is October 1, 2026, but MWCP has not yet opened the call: its listing reads 'ENTRY FORM COMING SOON' and no entry page exists on the site, so the fee, the image count and the submission link for Purple are not published yet. Watch the gallery's call-for-entries page for the form. — Deadline: October 1, 2026. Fee: See website. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: KG+SELECT 2027 · KYOTOGRAPHIE
item.description: Open call from KG+, the public art festival KYOTOGRAPHIE organises in Kyoto alongside its own International Photography Festival, for a solo exhibition proposal. Applicants must propose a solo show featuring photography or work incorporating photographic elements — moving image, installation and related media all count — and duos, collectives and collaborative groups are welcome. There is no theme, and fine art, conceptual, contemporary and documentary practices are all invited. Applications are open regardless of age, profession, nationality, experience, or whether an applicant is self-nominated or nominated by others; previously exhibited and unpublished work are equally eligible. A jury, to be announced, selects roughly ten finalists, each of whom receives a ¥200,000 production grant with no receipts required, around 20 square metres in a shared venue, and a place in the group exhibition running 17 April to 16 May 2027. During the festival the jury visits the exhibition and names one KG+SELECT Award winner, who receives a ¥500,000 production grant, a solo exhibition in the official programme of KYOTOGRAPHIE 2028, venue and production support, inclusion in the official catalogue and PR support; the jury may decline to give the award. Applications close 10 October 2026 at 23:59 JST and finalists are announced on the KG+ site in early December. The ¥10,000 fee is non-refundable and includes one KYOTOGRAPHIE 2027 festival passport per application. Applicants plan for a roughly 4 by 5 metre white cube and submit up to 20 images or a presentation video, a floor plan, an artist portrait and texts in both Japanese and English. Printing, framing, equipment rental, projector use, transport and installation are all at the artist's expense, and supervising the exhibition during the festival is the artist's responsibility, though one or two venue staff oversee the shared space and artists are not required to be present throughout. — Deadline: October 10, 2026. Fee: ¥10,000. Prize: ¥500,000 + Exhibition.

item.title: Guest Room: Claus Gunti & Visvaldas Morkevičius · Der Greif
item.description: The next edition of Der Greif's monthly curator-led open call, guest-curated by art historian and ECAL photography lecturer Claus Gunti and Lithuanian artist Visvaldas Morkevičius under the theme "Seeing with Emotions". The brief starts from the emotional churn of the feed — ASMR accounts, images of warfare, food porn and TikTok trends triggering overlapping and often paradoxical responses — and from images growing less credible as AI slop and templated content flood our timelines. Against that, the curators ask for work focused on the one thing we can claim to be real: our emotions. The topic is intentionally broad, taking in emotional states, care, coping mechanisms, intimacy, relationships with others and reflective practices. Up to five images per project may be submitted, plus video up to ten minutes. Selected work is published in an online showcase on Der Greif alongside emerging artists from all over the world, and selected artists also receive an online feedback session with the curators. Open to photographers and visual artists worldwide with no age or experience limits, though images already selected for a previous Der Greif opportunity cannot be re-submitted. Submission is through Picter and the fee is voluntary — Der Greif suggests a €10 donation but you may enter for free. Submissions open 25 August 2026. — Deadline: September 22, 2026. Fee: Free (suggested €10 donation). Prize: Publication + portfolio feedback.

item.title: Bon Voyage · New Hampshire Art Association
item.description: Member show at the New Hampshire Art Association's Portsmouth gallery built around travel, movement and how places shape us. NHAA encourages interpretations that range beyond photographic documentation of where you have been to reflect on how travel affects a sense of self and belonging, home, relationships, beliefs, cultural awareness and outlook — abstract and literal readings both welcome. Work may be in any medium that engages with travel, and NHAA names photography outright alongside painting, drawing, printmaking, mixed media, sculpture, installation, fibre arts and digital works. This is a juried member exhibition, lightly juried on space constraints, and it favours smaller-scale work up to 16 by 20 inches; each artist may enter one piece, created within the last three years and not previously shown at the Levy Gallery. Entry is $12 and current NHAA artist membership is required; membership is itself juried, with rolling digital applications reviewed by a panel of five jurors, results within 45 days, a $25 application fee and annual dues of $50–$125 on acceptance, so it is not something an artist can simply join into at the deadline. The show runs 30 September to 1 November 2026 at 136 State Street alongside Thor Art: A Retrospective by longtime member Bob Thoresen, with an opening reception on 2 October, 5–8pm; work is dropped off 27–28 September and collected 1–2 November. — Deadline: September 22, 2026. Fee: $12. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: ACTION! 2026 · Glasgow Gallery of Photography
item.description: Digital photography exhibition on the theme of action. "Photography has always been used to capture action, a protest, a celebration or sporting event" — the gallery is after the bride catching the bouquet, the winner crossing the finishing line, the moment made to be shared. The call is open across genres, naming sport photography, documentary and street photography among them, so long as the work meets the theme. This is a digital show rather than a print hang: selected work is displayed on screen in the Glasgow gallery from 4 to 28 November 2026 and on the gallery's YouTube channel, and also appears in an online gallery on the gallery's website and in an exhibition catalogue. Selected participants receive a digital certificate of participation, and photos and video of how the work is displayed are posted on the gallery's social media. Submission is free; photographers selected pay a £22 participation fee. Submit up to 8 JPEGs (300ppi, 1200 pixels minimum on the shortest side) by free file transfer to the gallery's submissions address — a lighter spec than the gallery's printed shows, which ask for 3000 pixels. Only selected photographers are notified. — Deadline: September 18, 2026. Fee: Free (£22 if accepted). Prize: Exhibition + publication.

item.title: Shape 2027 · Glasgow Gallery of Photography
item.description: International photography exhibition on shape. "Along with capturing light and shadow, photography is a great way to capture and explore shape" — man-made or found in nature, the gallery is after the silhouette, the architecture of a building, the geography around us, and what the right composition can make of them. Selected work is printed and displayed at the Glasgow Gallery of Photography from 7 to 30 January 2027, and also appears in an online gallery on the gallery's website and in an exhibition catalogue. Selected participants receive a digital certificate of participation, have their installed work photographed and filmed for the gallery's social media, and are automatically put forward for Photographer of the Month. Submission is free; photographers selected pay a £50 participation fee covering printing and installation, with prints presented in gallery-owned frames at 16"x12", 18"x12" or 12"x12" depending on the image. A discount is available to anyone selected for both January exhibitions. Submit up to 8 JPEGs (300ppi, 3000 pixels minimum on the shortest side) by free file transfer to the gallery's submissions address. Only selected photographers are notified. — Deadline: September 18, 2026. Fee: Free (£50 if accepted). Prize: Exhibition + publication.

item.title: Elements 2027 · Glasgow Gallery of Photography
item.description: International photography exhibition on the elements, which the gallery calls "the literally building blocks to the world around us" and leaves wide open to interpretation. That might be one or more of the four classical elements — earth, wind, water and fire — or the weather we live through and how it shapes our lives, or the elements as the building blocks of the universe, with the periodic table as a starting point. Selected work is printed and displayed at the Glasgow Gallery of Photography from 7 to 30 January 2027, and also appears in an online gallery on the gallery's website and in an exhibition catalogue. Selected participants receive a digital certificate of participation, have their installed work photographed and filmed for the gallery's social media, and are automatically put forward for Photographer of the Month. Submission is free; photographers selected pay a £50 participation fee covering printing and installation, with prints presented in gallery-owned frames at 16"x12", 18"x12" or 12"x12" depending on the image. A discount is available to anyone selected for both January exhibitions. Submit up to 8 JPEGs (300ppi, 3000 pixels minimum on the shortest side) by free file transfer to the gallery's submissions address. Only selected photographers are notified. — Deadline: September 18, 2026. Fee: Free (£50 if accepted). Prize: Exhibition + publication.

item.title: College Photographer of the Year 81
item.description: The 81st edition of the student photojournalism competition founded by Cliff and Vi Edom in 1945 and administered by the University of Missouri and the Reynolds Journalism Institute. Entry is free: CPOY credits co-sponsor Nikon Inc., “whose generosity allows CPOY to offer free entry to students in educational institutions worldwide.” Nineteen still-photography and multimedia categories are open to undergraduate and graduate students at any college, university or educational institution worldwide who enrolled for at least one semester, trimester or quarter between September 2025 and December 2026; anyone with two or more cumulative years of paid professional experience as a photographer, photo editor or videographer, including paid internships, is ineligible. Entries must have been created between August 23, 2025 and August 22, 2026. This is a journalistic competition — digital, analog/film or print alteration is prohibited outside the Illustration category, and AI-generated images are barred from every category, Illustration included. Awards include Nikon Z-series mirrorless camera and lens kits, a Missouri Photo Workshop fellowship, National Press Photographers Foundation monetary awards, Mountain Workshops and MediaStorm workshop tuition and a True/False Film Fest pass; the Alexia/CPOY Project Grant adds $1,000 to continue the proposed project, $500 for travel and lodging, and a place at The Alexia Fall Workshop. Judging runs October 17–24 and is livestreamed. — Deadline: September 21, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Nikon camera + workshop fellowships.

item.title: Color Effect · Orange County Center for Contemporary Art
item.description: OCCCA — an artist-run non-profit in the Santa Ana Artists Village, serving the community since 1980 — asks artists to treat colour as a force rather than decoration: something “coded with history, desire, identity, power, memory, and resistance” that “divides and unites, seduces, disrupts, obscures, and reveals.” The call wants ambitious proposals that embrace tension and contradiction, and names the practices it is looking for: “painting, installation, sculpture, photography, performance, video, sound, textiles, or interdisciplinary forms.” Juror Rachel Adams is Chief Curator and Director of Programs at the Bemis Center for Contemporary Arts, and has previously held roles at University at Buffalo Art Galleries, Oregon Contemporary and The Contemporary Austin; her curatorial practice sits at the intersections of photography, installation, sound, performance, video, new media and architecture. The call is open to all artists without regional restriction. Up to nine pieces may be entered — $45 covers the first three, then $15 per additional work. Accepted artists are notified January 8, 2027; the exhibition opens February 6, 2027 with a second reception on March 6 and closes March 20. Artwork is capped at 50 inches in any dimension including framing and 25 pounds, and OCCCA retains a 40% commission on sales. — Deadline: December 30, 2026. Fee: $45 (up to 3 works), $15 each additional. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: 31st Extremely Minnesota · Robbin Gallery
item.description: Robbin Gallery's long-running juried fine art exhibition for artists living and working in Minnesota, hung in the historic Robbinsdale Library gallery just north of Minneapolis. The media list is broad and explicit: “2D and 3D visual art forms including but not limited to painting, drawing, printmaking, sculpture, textile, photography, digital, mixed media” — video, performance and anything requiring an electrical hook-up are excluded, and generative AI “is not allowed in part or in whole.” Prints are welcome where that is normal for the medium, “as in photography, lithography, block-printing and digital.” Open to Minnesota residents aged 18 and over; entries must be original work completed within the last three years, not made under an instructor's supervision, and not previously exhibited at Robbin Gallery. $30 covers up to two pieces, with 2D work capped at 40 inches in any direction including frame. Cash awards totalling $1,000 are presented at the opening reception on Saturday, November 7, and the show runs November 6–29, 2026. The EntryThingy call opens Monday, August 31 at 9:00 am Central and closes Friday, October 9 at 11:59 pm Central; accepted work must be hand-delivered, as the gallery cannot accept shipped artwork. — Deadline: October 9, 2026. Fee: $30 (up to 2 works). Prize: $1,000 in cash awards.

item.title: Celebrate Art 2026 · Art League of Henderson County
item.description: The Art League of Henderson County's annual regional juried exhibition at Art Place Gallery in Hendersonville's Historic 7th Avenue District, with $2,500 in cash awards. Photography is both a submission category and an award category: alongside a $1,000 Best in Show, $250 category awards go to Work on Canvas or Panel, Work on Paper, Photography, Two-Dimensional Mixed Media, Three-Dimensional and Digital/AI Created Artwork, each with an honorable mention; fiber is also a submission category, though it is not named in the awards list. Juror Jane Allen Nodine is a Distinguished Professor Emerita and former Gallery Director at the University of South Carolina Upstate, an NEA/SECCA Southeastern Seven Fellowship recipient and a two-time South Carolina Arts Commission Artist Fellow; the awards judge, who selects from the installed exhibition, is announced at the opening event. Open to artists 18 and over residing in North Carolina, South Carolina, Georgia or Tennessee, with up to three original works for $40 — work made in instructional classes or workshops is not eligible. Entries are juried digitally from submitted images. Accepted work must be hand-delivered (shipped work is not accepted), all artwork must be offered for sale with a 30% commission to the League, and pieces stay on view through October 31 even if sold. The exhibition runs October 1–31, 2026 with an opening reception and awards on October 2. — Deadline: September 19, 2026. Fee: $40 (up to 3 works). Prize: $2,500 in cash awards.

item.title: Foodways · Cultural Council for Palm Beach County
item.description: The Cultural Council for Palm Beach County invites artists to interpret foodways — “the eating habits and culinary practices of the many cultures represented in the region” — for an exhibition running January 15 to March 6, 2027. The Council suggests three broad directions: growth and production practices and the people who cultivate, package and move food through the community; the role food plays in shaping identity, unity and tradition; and the environmental context of farming, fishing and food production. The submission guidelines enumerate media plainly — painting, sculpture, photography, works on paper, installations, digital art and video, crafts and textiles are all welcome — and each artist may submit up to five works with high-resolution images (two views for 3D) and a brief statement on how the work relates to the theme. Only artists who live in Palm Beach County, Florida are eligible. Applications are taken only through Artwork Archive, where a free account is enough to apply, and no entry fee is listed on either the Council's call page or the Artwork Archive listing. — Deadline: October 5, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: The Hopper Prize Fall 2026 Grants
item.description: The Hopper Prize's autumn cycle, awarding six unrestricted cash grants totalling $13,000: two of $4,500 and four of $1,000. The organisation runs bi-annually and gives $26,000 across the two cycles each year. Grants are open to artists aged 18 and over internationally, working in any media; the prize describes its remit as "the field of visual art in its broadest and most inclusive sense" and has funded photographers, painters, sculptors and video artists at every career stage since 2018. Alongside the six grants, a shortlist of 30 artists per cycle is archived on hopperprize.org with biographies and links, and applicants may opt in to additional exposure on the prize's Instagram feed. Applying is a two-step process: pay the $40 fee, then complete the application form, submitting up to 10 images. — Deadline: November 17, 2026. Fee: $40. Prize: $4,500.

item.title: Artist Residency — January–June 2027 · Kimmel Harding Nelson Center for the Arts
item.description: Kimmel Harding Nelson awards up to seventy-eight juried residencies a year to visual artists, writers, composers and interdisciplinary artists from across the United States and abroad, and this deadline fills the 2027 Session 1 window, January 4 to June 25 2027. Residencies run two to eight weeks and are entirely self-directed. Each resident gets a private bedroom and bathroom, a private studio and a $175 weekly stipend; writers and visual artists usually share an apartment with one other resident. Travel is the artist's own cost except the $100 cab fare from Omaha or Lincoln on arrival and departure, which the Kimmel Foundation pays. Selection is by a blind jury of external professionals who see only anonymous work samples and two anonymous statements — a statement of submitted works and a statement of intent — so names, credits, awards, universities, employers and gallery names must be stripped from every file. The work-sample guidelines state that "all types of visual art are accepted including but not limited to photography, painting, sculpture, ceramics, printmaking, mixed media, video, performance, drawing, or textiles", with the caveat that KHN does not hold facilities specific to every process. A number of "transitional" residencies are reserved for artists within two years of graduation, and a number are reserved each year for Nebraska artists. The $35 application fee cannot be waived; results are emailed by November 1. — Deadline: September 1, 2026. Fee: $35. Prize: 2–8 week residency + $175/week stipend.

item.title: Seen + Heard · The Dairy Barn Arts Center
item.description: Formerly Women of Appalachia, Seen + Heard is a regional exhibition bringing together women and people with diverse experiences of femininity to tell their stories through visual art and traditional craft. The Dairy Barn asks for work that challenges stereotypes, confronts marginalisation and celebrates the complexity of women's lives, feminine identities and gendered experience in Appalachia; jurors are told to weigh identity, belonging, resilience, visibility and social perception alongside originality, design, technique and craftsmanship, and to give priority to work that amplifies underrepresented perspectives. Accepted media are listed as collage, digital and new media, drawing, fibre arts, film and video, installation, mixed media, painting, performance, photography, pottery, printmaking, sculpture and traditional craft. One of the three jurors, Robyn Moore, is a photomedia artist and Associate Professor of Photography at Morehead State University who works in alternative and experimental photographic processes. $800 in prize money is awarded across an Outstanding Contribution award of $200, a $150 Voice and Visibility Award and three $150 Juror's Awards for Storytelling, Impact and Innovation. Each artist may submit up to three works completed on or after January 1 2024, and the entry fee is a self-selected sliding scale from $15 to $65 with no explanation required. The show runs January 23 to March 21 2027 in the Sauber Gallery; the Dairy Barn takes 35% on sales and artists pay shipping both ways. — Deadline: October 11, 2026. Fee: $15–$65 sliding scale. Prize: $800 in awards.

item.title: Solo Exhibition Proposals — Chaddock + Morrow Gallery · The Dairy Barn Arts Center
item.description: The Dairy Barn is choosing three artists for solo exhibitions in its Chaddock + Morrow Gallery through 2027, a roughly 400-square-foot space programmed to complement and extend the themes of the main galleries. Applicants propose a cohesive body of work — completed, in progress or planned — and are judged on artistic excellence, the strength of the proposal as a unified presentation, clarity of concept, suitability for the scale and character of the room, and whether the show can realistically be delivered on time. Accepted media are listed as collage, digital and new media, drawing, fibre arts, film and video, installation, mixed media, painting, photography, pottery, printmaking, sculpture and craft. The call is local: open to artists living in Athens, Meigs, Vinton, Hocking, Perry, Morgan and Washington counties in Ohio and Wood County in West Virginia, aged 18 and over, excluding anyone who has had a solo show at the Dairy Barn since January 1 2024. Applications ask for a 500-word artist statement, a 500-word exhibition proposal, a CV and a single PDF portfolio of 10 to 15 images, one work per page. The three 2027 slots run January 23 to March 21, May 29 to September 6, and October 2 to November 28; work may be listed not for sale, and the artist receives 65% of any sale. — Deadline: September 13, 2026. Fee: $10–$50 sliding scale. Prize: Solo exhibition.

item.title: Queensland Regional Art Awards 2026 · Flying Arts Alliance
item.description: Flying Arts Alliance's annual awards for artists living in regional and remote Queensland, outside the Brisbane City Council boundary. Flying Arts bills it as Australia's largest regional art awards prize pool and puts the total at A$326,800, but that figure counts the stated value of in-kind marketing, residencies and exhibitions alongside roughly A$62,500 in actual cash. There is no theme in 2026. The overall winner receives A$25,000 in non-acquisitive cash, a two-week solo show at Jan Manton Gallery in March 2027, a residency in Bundaberg and a print editorial profile. The Mervyn Moriarty Landscape Award adds A$10,000 plus a residency in Cairns and a solo show at FireWorks Gallery; the First Nations Artist Award is A$10,000; the Remote Artist, Emerging Artist and Young Artist awards are A$5,000 each, and the two People's Choice awards are A$1,500 and A$1,000. Entries close at 3pm on 18 September and finalists are announced on 15 October, with the winners named in person at the Gala Awards Night in Brisbane on 26 November. Artists must be 15 or over; work must be original, completed in 2026, and must not have previously won a major state, national or international prize. Size limits are 120 × 120cm and under 10kg for framed 2D work, and digital work must run under five minutes. Finalists must make the work available through 2027 for the statewide touring exhibition and deliver it to the Brisbane office at their own cost. AI may be used only as a tool: Flying Arts states that AI must not be "the substantive final result, presented as the work, regardless of medium", entrants must declare this and describe every AI tool used, and works in breach are not eligible for awards. A 20% commission applies to sales. — Deadline: September 18, 2026. Fee: A$40 (A$35 members, A$25 ages 15–25). Prize: A$25,000 + Solo exhibition + Residency.

item.title: Mayor's Art Show 2027 · City of Eugene Cultural Services
item.description: Eugene's long-running annual exhibition of local artistic excellence, staged at the Hult Center for the Performing Arts from January 11 to February 26 2027 and opening the night of the city's State of the City address. Entry is free and each artist or collective may submit one work, completed after January 1 2025. Eight $500 awards are given: Mayor's 2D Choice, Mayor's 3D Choice, Jurors' 2D Choice, Jurors' 3D Choice, People's Choice, Curator's Choice, Hult Center's Choice and Best Depiction of Eugene. A curated selection then moves to the City Hall Gallery from April to July 2027. Applicants must live in Eugene, work in Eugene, or have a strong connection to Eugene and its land, and be 18 or older; the city runs a separate Teen Mayor's Art Show through Maude Kerns Art Center. Selection criteria are conceptual strength, artistry, innovation and diversity of materials and art practices. Two-dimensional work is capped at 72 by 60 inches framed and must arrive hang-ready with a wire and D-rings; digital video and sound submissions may run up to eight minutes. Artists set their own price and receive 70% of any sale. Optional application information sessions and one-to-one technical assistance run through late September. — Deadline: September 30, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $500.

item.title: Bi-Annual Open Call 2027 · GALLERY jENSEITS
item.description: GALLERY jENSEITS is a contemporary gallery that opened in May 2026 at 1101 Saint Gregory Street in Mt. Adams, Cincinnati, and describes itself as showing "both the renowned and the unknown, the alluring and the absurd". Its first bi-annual open call selects work for the 2027 exhibition programme, which runs from February to September 2027 in shows of six to ten weeks. There is no application fee. The call is open internationally to emerging and established artists working in contemporary art, and the gallery's media list is explicit: "All media are accepted, including (but not limited to) painting, sculpture, installation, ceramics, printmaking, photography, fiber arts, digital, and new media." Applicants must be 18 or over, submit high-quality images with descriptions, pricing, dimensions, creation dates and materials, and be able to deliver and retrieve work by shipping or in person; up to 18 pieces may be submitted. Selected work must be available for the full six- or ten-week run and arrive ready to install. Artists are responsible for shipping costs and insurance in both directions, and the gallery makes final curatorial decisions. — Deadline: September 15, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Urban & Pop Art Exhibition · Bee Cave Arts Foundation
item.description: Juried exhibition at the Bee Cave Arts Foundation gallery in the Texas Hill Country outside Austin, celebrating work “inspired by city life, popular culture, fashion, music, advertising, graphic design, comics, typography, and the imagery that shapes our everyday world”. The prospectus is open to artists working in all art mediums, photography included, and the exhibit is open to Central Texas artists. Juror and curator J Muzacz is an Austin public artist and mosaicist who co-founded The Mosaic Workshop in East Austin. One fee covers up to three entries; work must be original, wired and ready to hang, and for sale, with a 30% donation to the foundation on any sale. The show runs October 10 – November 6, 2026, with a reception on October 10, 2–4pm. — Deadline: September 3, 2026. Fee: $45 ($35 members). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Lure of the Local 5: Love Letters · Mundelein Arts Commission
item.description: Fifth edition of the Mundelein Arts Commission's annual juried exhibition, which takes its name from Lucy Lippard's The Lure of the Local and this year runs on the theme Love Letters. It is free to apply and free to participate, artists of any medium and skill level are encouraged, and the show is built around “artists who live and work among us – our teachers, neighbors, friends, and fellow community members”. Awards are a $150 Critic's Choice with three honourable mentions, a $150 People's Choice with a runner-up, and a MAC 10th Anniversary Purchase Award; the commission is also taking separate email proposals for participatory installation works. The exhibition runs October 16 – November 22, 2026 at the Archer Business Center in downtown Mundelein, open Saturdays and Sundays 11am–5pm with weekend workshops and live music, and opens with a reception on October 16 that typically draws 400–500 visitors. — Deadline: August 30, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $300 in awards + Purchase Award.

item.title: The Dark Side of Art · Gulf Coast Artists' Alliance
item.description: Juried exhibition at GCAA ArtWorks, the St. Petersburg storefront gallery and studio space of the Gulf Coast Artists' Alliance, a volunteer-staffed 501(c)(3) founded in 2006. The theme looks at how artists use macabre, gothic and unsettling imagery to confront human fear, psychological pain and social taboo; the call invites “the macabre and gothic, subconscious and trauma, the devil and evil, or a personal emotional struggle”, and says all interpretations of the theme are welcome. Photography is one of the accepted categories and the call is open to US-based artists. The exhibition runs October 8 – November 7, 2026, with a Halloween-themed reception on Saturday October 10 and a Day of the Dead celebration with a costume contest on Sunday November 1. — Deadline: September 13, 2026. Fee: $20. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Nocefresca Open Call 2027
item.description: Seventh edition of a rural artist residency in Milis, a village of citrus groves at the foot of the Montiferru range in western Sardinia, 19 km from the coast. Month-long residencies run March–June and September–December 2027, with 42 places across the year and up to seven residents at a time; the residency closes in January, February, July and August. Photographers are named among those it is for, alongside visual artists, designers, writers, composers, videomakers, illustrators and architects, and no final outcome is required. Each group is accompanied by a guest curator across two group meetings and three one-to-one sessions, with a public open studio at the end of the month. The residency is self-funded and cannot offer fellowships: studio-and-housing fees run €1,650–€1,880 a month depending on studio and room, and selection weighs artistic quality, feasibility of the project, length of stay, impact on the group and the local community, and secured budget. Applying is free; a €450 confirmation fee falls due within two weeks of selection. — Deadline: September 7, 2026. Fee: Free (€1,650–€1,880/month if selected). Prize: Residency.

item.title: No Limits 2026 — Golden Duck Gallery
item.description: Golden Duck Gallery's annual birthday show, an open-topic international open call in central Budapest, a few hundred metres from the Great Market Hall. Physical and digital painting, photography, mixed media, sculpture and installation are all welcome; the constraints are price caps (€1,000 for work up to 60×60 cm, €4,000 up to 100×100 cm, none for 3D) and a ready-to-hang requirement. Submitting up to five works is free, and selected artists then decide whether to exhibit and pay an exhibition fee of €70 for one work, €100 for two or €120 for three, covering all exhibition services for the four-week run; the jury also picks three Curator's Pick works that exhibit free, and artists aged 14–25 are juried separately and exhibit free of charge. A €1,000 prize fund is split across a €200 Excellence Prize and €150 each for the Concept and Talent Awards. Work can also be shown digitally on screens in New York, Vienna and Budapest. The exhibition runs October 6 – November 14, 2026, opening October 9 at 6pm. — Deadline: September 6, 2026. Fee: Free (€70–€120 if accepted). Prize: €1,000 prize fund.

item.title: Field Notes from the Middle · Filter Photo
item.description: Inaugural juried exhibition at Filter Space, Filter Photo's Chicago gallery, surveying contemporary photography across the Midwest. The call is open to photography, photographic materials and other lens-based artwork that engages with the region, from artists making work in Illinois, Indiana, Iowa, Kansas, Michigan, Minnesota, Missouri, Nebraska, North Dakota, Ohio, South Dakota and Wisconsin. Juror Nathaniel M. Stein, Curator of Photography at the Cincinnati Art Museum, will select five artists to each exhibit five to seven works from a single body of work, and all five are eligible for the 2026 Filter Photo Museum Purchase Award of $2,000, with the selected work acquired by the Cincinnati Art Museum for its permanent collection. Applicants submit an artist statement of 500 words or less, a current bio and 15–20 sample images. Accepted artists are notified in mid-to-late October, work is due at Filter Space by November 25, and the exhibition runs December 4, 2026 – February 13, 2027 with a gallery reception on opening night. — Deadline: September 30, 2026. Fee: $35. Prize: $2,000 Museum Purchase Award.

item.title: Feria de Fotografía y Afines 2026 · Freezer Festival Internacional de Fotografía
item.description: The editorial fair at the third Freezer International Photography Festival in La Plata, Argentina, held under the edition's theme Lo real. Photographers, collectives, publishers, small presses and photography-adjacent projects are invited to bring fanzines, prints, photobooks and photographic objects to a two-day market at the Edificio Karakachoff's Espacio Dickinson on Friday November 13 and Sunday November 15, with free public entry. The festival frames it as “un gesto de comunidad” — a place to make projects visible and build networks beyond the screen. Stands are a 90×90 cm table with two chairs at ARS 50,000 a day, a self-supplied clothes rail at ARS 40,000, or both at ARS 65,000; stands for the UNLP university photography programme are free, and payment is by local transfer or PayPal from abroad. Applications close September 14 or when places run out, and selected projects are announced September 18. — Deadline: September 14, 2026. Fee: ARS 40,000+. Prize: Exhibition booth.

item.title: BINGO 2026 · Candela Photographic Arts
item.description: A pilot “give two, get one” open call from Candela, the Richmond photography gallery and book publisher that became a 501(c)(3) in 2026 after fifteen years as Candela Books + Gallery. Fifteen small photographic works are selected for a show running October 2–24 that ends in a bingo fundraiser: each framed print on view goes home with a winner on closing day, while a second print from each artist enters a randomised swap that sends another participant's work back to them, with Candela covering the postage. There is no theme other than the use of photography and no entry fee; artists may submit up to three prints, each with at least two available editions and none larger than 12 inches on the longest side. Candela frames and mats the exhibited works and prints are due by September 22. The gallery is candid that the show is philanthropic and community-focused and “may not be a great fit for artists looking for big sales opportunities”. — Deadline: August 28, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition + print swap.

item.title: Photography Exhibition 2026 · Gutman Gallery
item.description: Gutman Gallery's only single-medium exhibition of the year, run by The Guild of Artists & Artisans in downtown Ann Arbor. The call carries the gallery's ongoing storytelling theme into a question for photographers — “What compels one to take photographs? Is it to share stories, to seek connection?” — and asks for work that captures each photographer's own reason for using the medium, explained in the artist statement. Photographers of all subject matter and all formats may enter as long as the work can be displayed in a gallery; 2D work must be wired and ready to hang, and artists must be able to document their process and verify authorship. One entry fee covers up to three works, with two images allowed per work. Editing software is fine provided all imagery originates from the artist's own creative source, but work composed entirely by or relying on AI-generated imagery is ineligible. Jury decisions go out September 4–5, accepted work is delivered September 9–19, and the exhibition runs September 26 – October 31, 2026 with an opening reception on the 26th. The Guild takes 30% commission from members and 40% from non-members on sales. — Deadline: September 2, 2026. Fee: $40 ($20 members). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Brightwork Grants 2027 · Anchorlight
item.description: Two grants from the Brightwork Foundation, the funder behind Anchorlight's Brightwork Fellowship in Raleigh, open to visual artists living full time in any North Carolina county. One $2,000 Professional Development Grant supports workshops, classes, conferences or one-to-one technical instruction, professional documentation of a portfolio, a designer-built website, or equipment and studio materials. One $3,000 Studio Project Grant supports the production of studio-based work, including equipment, research expenses specific to the project, and costs tied to a confirmed future solo exhibition in a public gallery. Applicants choose one grant and submit a proposed budget with a statement of intent or project description, artist statement, bio and recent work; awardees must provide receipts for each purchase. Eligibility is visual artists 21 and over who have lived in North Carolina for at least twelve consecutive months and will stay for the grant period, and who are not enrolled in an undergraduate or graduate degree programme during it — doctoral candidates who have finished coursework may apply. Funds must be used between January and December 2027, and you may not apply for a grant and the Brightwork Fellowship in the same cycle. — Deadline: August 28, 2026. Fee: $10. Prize: $2,000–$3,000.

item.title: 28th International Open · Woman Made Gallery
item.description: Woman Made Gallery invites submissions for its 28th International Open, a juried exhibition showcasing work in all media by women and non-binary artists from around the world, and says it is inviting works that explore and push conceptual and material boundaries. The show runs February 27 to March 27, 2027 at the gallery's Halsted Street space in Chicago; entries are due December 18, 2026 and artists are notified January 15, 2027. The juror is listed as TBA and the entry form link had not gone up when this call was posted — the gallery says it will follow shortly. The $30 fee covers one submission per artist of one to three artworks. Woman Made offers around 30 fee waivers per juried exhibition, 15 of them reserved for ALAANA/BIPOC and/or LGBTQIA+ artists, granted on a rolling basis for financial instability or low-income status, student or recent-graduate status, or other demonstrated need; members at the Enhanced Artist level and above receive one free entry a year. The gallery welcomes art from all women, including trans women and femme/feminine-identifying genderqueer and non-binary artists. Work previously shown at Woman Made cannot be resubmitted, and pieces may not exceed six feet horizontally or 75 pounds unless the artist delivers and collects them; video, sound and digital works need presentation instructions. Artists may use AI tools for research or inspiration, but submissions consisting of AI-generated images, text or objects with minimal human intervention will not be included. — Deadline: December 18, 2026. Fee: $30. Prize: Group exhibition.

item.title: Seeing Red · Epperson Gallery
item.description: A juried winter exhibition built on the colour red at Epperson Gallery in Crockett, California, juried by Donna Seager, who ran Donna Seager Gallery in San Rafael from 2005, co-founded Seager Gray Gallery in Mill Valley in 2011, and now runs Donna Seager Fine Arts & Artists' Books. The call reads red as humanity's oldest and most primordial pigment and asks for work that subverts, celebrates and explores its history — prehistoric ochre and Renaissance vermilion, the scarlet of Roman emperors and Catholic cardinals, the banners of political uprising, and the pure red of Eastern bridal wear and protective talismans. Photography is named outright in the accepted mediums, alongside sculpture, painting, mixed media, collage, drawing and fiber arts, and photographs must be signed and numbered on the front. Read the medium rules together, though: the same prospectus bars digitally rendered, digitally altered or digitally printed work, along with giclées, offset lithographs and reproductions of any kind, so this is a call for hand-made prints rather than inkjet output. Awards are $1,500, $1,000 and $500. Entry is open to artists 18 and over residing in the USA; work must be one of a kind, for sale, not previously shown at Epperson, no wider than 60 inches or heavier than 60 pounds, and ready to hang with D-rings and wire — sawtooth hangers are refused and three-dimensional work must be hand-delivered. The gallery retains a 50% commission on all sales and asks artists to price their submissions to reflect that split. AI-generated, assisted or enhanced work is not accepted. Applicants hear back October 12, shipped work must arrive by November 6, and the show runs November 14 to December 27, 2026 with a reception on opening day. Epperson held its 30th anniversary party in April 2026; its own exhibitions page now lists the show for November 14 to December 27, 2026, while the call terms and entry run through CaFÉ. — Deadline: October 6, 2026. Fee: $40 (1 image), $10 each additional. Prize: $1,500 / $1,000 / $500 + exhibition.

item.title: Arts Retreat Residency · New York Mills Regional Cultural Center
item.description: A rural arts organisation in west-central Minnesota, founded as the New York Mills Arts Retreat in 1990 and expanded into a regional cultural center in 1992, hosts one artist at a time in a one-bedroom bungalow three blocks south of downtown, with studio access at the Cultural Center. Housing and studio use cost nothing and the application is free. Residencies run two to six weeks. There are two deadlines a year — April 1 for July to December stays and October 1 for January to June — and applications are accepted year round. The centre welcomes artists from all disciplines, naming performance, literary, audio and visual media, and selects on artistic merit, dedication to their craft, commitment to creative growth and interest in developing community through the arts. No stipend is offered and residents provide their own transportation and meals; the house deliberately has no television, computer or car, and staff or community members will collect artists from Perham or Wadena. Each resident creates and leads one community outreach programme — a workshop, reading, performance or other interactive event at the Cultural Center — and can develop it with Artistic Director Megan Shirley-Ross or partner with the local schools, senior center or library. Applicants are notified within 30 to 45 days after the deadline. Note that the previous round was extended from October 1 to October 15, so the window may move again, but October 1 is the published date. — Deadline: October 1, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Free 2–6 week residency.

item.title: Corsicana Artist and Writer Residency 2027
item.description: Two-month, fully funded studio residencies at 100 West, an unaltered 1890s Odd Fellows lodge in downtown Corsicana, fifty miles south of Dallas. Six artists and three writers are accepted for 2027 - two artists and one writer per term - across Winter (January 4 to February 23), Spring (March 1 to April 27) and Fall (October 11 to December 7). Residents are given a private furnished studio with lodging: the second- and third-floor artist studios are 2,400 square feet each, with twelve- and thirteen-foot ceilings, long drywall work walls, an intaglio press and large utility sinks. The residency also provides professional documentation of the work in photo and video, a mid-term studio visit from a regional professional, introductions to the Dallas/Fort Worth cultural network, complimentary rides to and from the Dallas airports, bicycles, and access to digital projectors, construction tools and a wood shop. Residents give a twenty-minute presentation on the second Thursday of the term and hold open studios on the last Saturday; optional studio visits with MFA students in Dallas, followed by a presentation, carry a $500 honorarium. Open to artists of international, United States and Texas origin, with applications limited to one person per studio. Ceramic, fiberglass and aerosol-based work cannot be accommodated, and sound-based work is generally not hosted, so applicants working with sound are asked to enquire first. Artists submit five examples of work and two references; the application fee is $30, and accepted applicants pay a one-time, non-refundable $200 administration fee by November 1, 2026. 179 artists and writers from the United States and eighteen countries have been hosted since 2012, and the 2026 cohort opened with the Vienna-based alternative-process photographer Kaja Clara Joo. Families and pets are not accommodated, and 100 West is reached only by a steep staircase. — Deadline: September 1, 2026. Fee: $30 (+$200 admin fee if selected). Prize: Fully funded 2-month residency.

item.title: Exhibition Proposals · Holter Museum of Art
item.description: The Holter Museum of Art in Helena, Montana mounts twenty to twenty-five solo and group exhibitions a year across three main galleries and two smaller ones, each running six to twelve weeks, and fills part of that programme from artist proposals reviewed on a rolling quarterly basis. The museum sets four selection dates a year; the next is September 9, 2026, with proposals due September 6, and the final 2026 round closes December 6 for a December 9 review. Applicants hear back within two weeks of the selection date, but the museum organises exhibitions one to three years in advance, so a successful proposal is not a near-term show. A proposal takes a cover letter giving the exhibition title and a description of the concept, content and medium along with the method of delivery; an artist statement and biography, each kept to a page; a CV; an image list with titles, dimensions, dates and media; any educational programming or community outreach on offer; and a budget - the museum asks applicants to plan for shipping, which it calls the largest cost artists currently face. Ten labelled high-quality images are required and up to twenty are accepted, with an optional audio/visual upload. The application form charges a $20 fee on its second step. The museum shows photography as a matter of course: the current Baucus Gallery solo, Jessica Hays's The Sun Sets Midafternoon, runs August 21 to October 11, 2026 and is by a Montana photographer working in pigment printing, handmade artist books, video, and historic and experimental photographic processes. — Deadline: September 6, 2026. Fee: $20. Prize: Solo or group exhibition.

item.title: William Flanagan Memorial Creative Persons Center — Winter/Spring 2027 · Edward F. Albee Foundation
item.description: Edward Albee founded this residency in 1962 with the proceeds of Who's Afraid of Virginia Woolf?, and the foundation has run it ever since at the William Flanagan Memorial Creative Persons Center - known to everyone as The Barn - a converted horse stable on a secluded knoll about two miles from the centre of Montauk and the Atlantic. After a renovation completed in the early 2020s it now operates nearly year-round and houses four people at a time, usually two visual artists and two writers, each with an en-suite bedroom and a separate private studio, plus a shared library, eat-in kitchen and patio. Residencies run for whole calendar months only; no partial stays, and no four-week block straddling two months. This application window covers residencies from January to June 2027 (the Barn closes every December). Selection is made, in the foundation's words, using only talent and need as criteria, and the call is open to any creative person over 18 of any nationality, students included. There is no application fee and no cost of any kind to stay. Domestic Fellows receive a $2,500 stipend on completing the residency; international Fellows are reimbursed for expenses up to the same amount. Visual arts applicants submit 6 to 12 images and/or up to three media files with a CV, an artist's statement setting out the proposed project, and the email addresses of two professional referees, whom the foundation contacts itself. Photography sits squarely inside the visual-arts stream: the current fellows include Becca Albee, whose work is anchored in photography, Robin Crookall, a NYSCA/NYFA Artist Fellow in Photography, and the lens-based artist Caroline Minchew, whose photographs are held in the National Gallery of Art Photograph Study Collection. — Deadline: September 14, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $2,500 stipend + month-long residency.

item.title: 2028 Gallery Exhibition Season · Garrison Art Center
item.description: Garrison Art Center is a 501(c)(3) on Garrison's Landing, directly across the Hudson from West Point, and it programmes its two galleries a full season ahead. This call is for the 2028 season and takes proposals for solo shows, two- and three-person shows and small curated group exhibitions; proposals are paired so that both rooms are filled at once, with each accepted proposal placed in either the 625-square-foot Gillette Gallery or the 360-square-foot Balter Gallery, while the Visiting Artist gets both. Photography is one of the seven media the centre lists on its own prospectus, alongside mixed media, sculpture, painting, drawing and printmaking; the current ROOTS exhibition in the galleries includes cyanotype, which the centre describes as a camera-less photographic process. Applicants are US residents aged 18 or over with a studio within a 90-minute radius of Garrison, NY - the centre is candid that this is about logistics rather than prestige: artists deliver and collect their own work, must attend the opening reception, and the gallery coordinator and committee prefer to curate the show from an in-person studio visit, though Zoom is possible. Group proposals pay once and apply once, with individual CVs but a single unified proposal and the images divided between the artists. Five to ten work samples are required. A jury of ten reviews everything over several rounds, a deliberate process the centre says takes several months, so expect to hear back no earlier than May 2027. Applications open August 15, 2026 and close January 15, 2027; the application fee is $30. — Deadline: January 15, 2027. Fee: $30. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Creative Catalyst Fellowship 2027 · AAPI Civic Engagement Fund
item.description: The AAPI Civic Engagement Fund gives up to eight artists $30,000 each to make work that engages the public on issues facing Asian American and Pacific Islander communities. The 2027 theme is Belonging, which the Fund defines as a sense of community, home, agency and the essential right for communities to flourish - a counterweight to racism and violence, and a way of recognising how AAPI communities have shaped this country. Photography is named outright among the funded forms, alongside printmaking, illustration and modular installations, with digital and media-based work, written and narrative forms, and hybrid or interdisciplinary projects also eligible; the Fund says it is drawn to work that is portable and reproducible, and cannot fund feature-length film, fully staged theatre, dance, event-based work needing rehearsal infrastructure, or projects that depend on large-scale or fixed installations. As a nonpartisan nonprofit it also cannot fund work advocating for or against a candidate. It is a yearlong programme running January to December 2027: fellows attend a virtual orientation, a required two-day in-person retreat on February 16-18, 2027 with travel and accommodation covered, virtual check-ins, and submit a narrative report, with finished artwork due August 15, 2027 and promotion running to December. Beyond the money, the Fund provides a communications consultant, digital advertising, introductions to AAPI organisations, help placing the work in galleries and venues experienced with social-justice art, and production of posters, books and other replicas. Artists keep ownership; the Fund takes the right to reproduce the work for its charitable activities. Applying is free, through a Google Form, with up to five work samples in a single PDF. Open to individual artists 18 or over based in the United States - organisations are not eligible and international applicants cannot apply, though US citizenship is not required. Two optional information webinars run on September 1 and September 4, 2026. — Deadline: October 15, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: 8 × $30,000.

item.title: AAP Magazine #61 Street · All About Photo
item.description: The 61st printed issue of AAP Magazine takes street photography as its theme, and All About Photo wants a cohesive body of work rather than one-off frames: photographs are judged individually in a first round, then as a unified group as they could appear on the page. The brief is deliberately wide - documentary, conceptual, experimental, digital and analog processes are all welcome, in black and white, colour or monochrome - and the call reaches back to Atget, Kertesz, Abbott, Cartier-Bresson, Frank, Arbus, Maier, Winogrand and Friedlander for its frame of reference. Twenty-five photographers are selected: the top three take $500, $300 and $200 and the next twenty-two are Merit Award winners, with every winner published in the printed Volume 61, sent a free copy, and given a permanent place in the online Winners Gallery. First place also gets an interview. Open worldwide to anyone 18 or over, professional or amateur; images already published in AAP Magazine cannot be resubmitted. Entry is $30 for the first three images and $5 for each additional one through September 8, after which the base fee rises to $35. Judging runs October 3 to November 15 and winners are notified around November 30, 2026. — Deadline: September 29, 2026. Fee: $30–$35. Prize: $500/$300/$200 + Publication.

item.title: Personal Best · Ashton Gallery @ Art on 30th
item.description: A San Diego regional juried show at Ashton Gallery inside the Art on 30th art centre in North Park, on view October 3 - 30, 2026 and juried by painting instructor and professional artist Tracie Fearing. The brief is deliberately open rather than thematic: most artists have one piece they consider their best, and the gallery wants that work as a deeply personal measure of growth and achievement. Photography is explicitly welcomed alongside all 2D work and any 3D work that fits on a pedestal, and fabric and journal pages are accepted if prepared for hanging; the gallery does not take AI-created artwork, digital art, installations, reproductions or giclee prints, with an exception that keeps limited-edition photographic and printmaking editions eligible. Enter online or drop work off in person - the jurors often prefer to see submissions in person, and photographic entries should be printed by the deadline because accepted online entries must reach the gallery on Monday September 28 between 11am and 2pm. Work must be wired with two D-rings and ready to hang, signed and labelled on the reverse with title, size and medium, and offered for sale; anything marked NFS is juried out and the gallery takes the standard 50% commission on sales. Opening reception Saturday October 3, 4-7pm. — Deadline: September 25, 2026. Fee: $35 up to 2, $45 up to 4, $55 up to 6. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Boost Grants 2026 · Helpmann Academy
item.description: A$500 micro-grants for emerging South Australian creatives, made possible through the generosity of John Phillips. The money is meant to cover the ordinary costs that stall a young practice: purchasing, hiring or upgrading technology and equipment, where the Academy names cameras and associated equipment among the eligible buys; training that helps you develop or adapt your practice; workshops and seminars; materials and tools, including printing and framing; operational costs such as studio rental, website hosting and insurance; and audience-development costs such as paid advertising, posters and social media strategists. Photography is one of the Visual Arts specialisations on the application form, sitting between Installation and Moving Image. Applications are invited from graduates of supported creative degrees at Adelaide University and Flinders University, and from graduates of the former University of South Australia and University of Adelaide, for up to five years from 31 December of their final year of study; honours students qualify only where honours followed directly from the undergraduate degree, master's and PhD candidates only through their earlier study, and final-year students are not eligible for this round. There is no application fee. The form asks for a two-page artist CV, an official academic transcript, a budget on the Academy's own template and four to six images or one to two audio-visual demos, alongside written answers on your practice and on how the funds would boost it. Assessment weighs alignment with career development, feasibility and value, potential impact, and capacity to build new networks, collaborations or partnerships. Funded activity must take place between 1 January and 31 December 2027, the panel may award less than the sum requested, and there is no retrospective funding for work already begun. — Deadline: August 31, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: A$500.

item.title: Elise Ross Regional Award 2027 · Helpmann Academy
item.description: Up to A$5,000 for an emerging creative based in, or making work in, regional South Australia. The award was established by the Ross Family in memory of Elise Ross and exists to offset what distance and small local populations cost an artist early on: it aims to foster creative activity in the regions and to build connections between emerging creatives and regional audiences. Two routes are open. Artists and collectives living in regional South Australia may propose activity in or outside the region, and may use the money for residencies, specialised training or workshop participation, exhibitions, mentorships, internships or self-directed projects. Artists living in metropolitan areas must undertake the activity in regional South Australia and demonstrate a genuine connection to that region or its community; touring, community art projects and workshops are added to their list of eligible activities. Photography is one of the Visual Arts specialisations on the application form. Applicants must be final-year students or graduates within five years of a supported creative degree at Adelaide University, which now includes the former University of South Australia and University of Adelaide, or at Flinders University; honours study counts where it followed directly from the undergraduate degree, and master's and PhD candidates qualify only through their earlier study. There is no application fee. The application asks for three written responses of 500 words or less, plus a further response specific to whether you are regionally or metropolitan based, an artist CV, an official academic transcript showing the conferral date, a budget on the Academy's template with notes, a proposal timeline and three to five images or one to two audio-visual demos. Funded activity must take place between 1 January and 31 December 2027, and applicants are notified of outcomes within four weeks of the closing date. — Deadline: September 15, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: A$5,000.

item.title: VIVID '26: A Juried National Exhibit of LOUD, BOLD & VIBRANT Artworks · d'Art Center
item.description: d'Art Center's annual colour show fills the main gallery of the Norfolk nonprofit with work that is, in the organisers' words, exceptionally vibrant, bold, loud and brilliant in colour — they want visitors to walk into an explosion of it. The call is national and open to all mediums, 2D and 3D, functional and non-functional, fine art and fine art craft, in every style; photography is welcome and d'Art runs a dedicated photography show, Contrive, in its vault space over the same weeks. Entrants must be 18 or older and living in the United States, and work must have been made in the last eight years, weigh under 50 pounds and measure no more than 60 inches in its longest dimension, though the Gallery Director can waive the size and weight limits by prior arrangement. Entry is $35 for three submissions — three images is the minimum, so a single piece can be entered three times or padded out with detail shots — and each further work is $5, to a cap of ten. Gallery Director Amanda Bradley curates the selection alongside a guest juror, still to be named, who picks the award winners: $500, $300 and $150. The exhibition runs 31 October to 5 December 2026 with a reception on 6 November shared with Contrive, and is archived permanently on d'Art's online archive site. Sales split 60/40 in the artist's favour; artists arrange their own shipping and must include a prepaid FedEx or UPS return label. — Deadline: September 20, 2026. Fee: $35 (3 works), $5 each additional. Prize: $500 / $300 / $150 + Exhibition.

item.title: Small Expressions 2026 · Northwind Art
item.description: Northwind Art's juried show for the giving season asks what an artist can do inside sixteen inches. Everything shown — frame and mount included — has to fit within that in any direction, and the organisers call it one diverse exhibit, welcoming entries in all mediums and naming photography first in the list. All work must be for sale, and the show is run differently from most: rather than hanging everything for the full run, one to three works per artist are on the wall at a time with more held in backstock, and a piece is replaced as soon as it sells. Two Northwind Art curators, the local artists Kim Kopp and Anne Hirondelle, judge on quality, professionalism and sales potential, and one $250 Jurors' Choice Award is given. Up to seven images may be entered for a single $35 fee — per artist, not per work — and that fee is waived on the honour system, using the code DISCOUNT, for artists from historically underrepresented BIPOC and LGBTQIA+ communities. No AI-derived imagery. Accepted work must be delivered in person to the Jeanette Best Gallery at 701 Water Street in Port Townsend; the gallery will not accept shipped work or ship unsold work back, so this is realistically a regional call. The exhibition runs 19 November 2026 to 4 January 2027. — Deadline: September 24, 2026. Fee: $35 (free for BIPOC and LGBTQIA+ artists). Prize: $250 + Exhibition.

item.title: Chase Gallery 2027 Season · Spokane Arts
item.description: Spokane Arts is taking portfolios for the 2027 exhibition schedule of the Chase Gallery, the city-owned space on the lower level of Spokane City Hall next to the council chambers, free and open whenever the building is. The gallery's stated mission is to show work that engages the public, brings people to a new outlook on contemporary issues and gives people of all backgrounds space to share a perspective; two-dimensional, sculptural, installation, video, audio, traditional and experimental work are all encouraged, and the Chase has given over its walls to photography before, including a forty-three-year retrospective of Rick Singer's Spokane pictures. Individual artists, artist teams and guest curators proposing a themed group show are all eligible. The gallery mainly curates group exhibits out of individual applications, but exceptionally strong work may be considered for a solo show. Applicants must live in Washington, Oregon, Idaho or Montana, with priority given to residents of the Intermountain Northwest. There is no entry fee. The application asks for an artist statement, a CV, a numbered works list with title, dimensions, year and medium, and between five and ten work samples; video may be linked instead, up to ten minutes in total. AI-generated, AI-prompted and AI-assisted work is barred outright and digital submissions are run through an AI image detector. The gallery takes 30 percent on sales and artists arrange their own shipping and delivery. — Deadline: September 7, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Gallery exhibition.
